metas.name: Albania - Bollard
metas.note:
Albanian bollards are triangular in shape, and white with a black top. They have a red front and a white rear reflector.

NOTE: Italy uses the same bollards.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/albania.

metas.name: Andorra - Bollard
metas.note:
The Andorran bollard has an orange reflector and can be occasionally found on the main highways.

NOTE: This bollard can also be found in Spain.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/andorra.

metas.name: Australia - Bollard
metas.note:
Australian bollards are white with a red reflector on the front and grey on the back.

Turkish bollards are similar but lack a back reflector. If unsure, check the sun position, landscape, or vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - WA stripy Bollard
metas.note: These black-and-white stripy bollards are unique to Western Australia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Austria - Bollard
metas.note:
Austria uses white bollards, with a black top. The colour of the reflector is (dark) red or dark grey.

  • Many bollards also feature a small nipple-shaped black cap on the top. Bollards sometimes have a snow pole on top.

NOTE: Slovenia and Montenegro use the same bollards, but with bright red reflectors instead of grey or dark red. Germany uses simple white bollards with grey reflectors.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/austria.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Bollard
metas.note:
Bangladesh uses red-and-white concrete bollards throughout the whole country.

NOTE: They can also be found in a square form instead of a circular form.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Belgium - Bollard
metas.note:
Belgium uses white bollards with a yellow rectangular reflector on the front and white on the back. A second type of bollard is dark brown with two red stripes at the top. Occasionally, other bollards can be seen.

NOTE: Denmark uses similar white bollards, but they have a red stripe at the top and the reflector is not rectangular. The dark brown bollard with two red stripes can also be seen in the Netherlands.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/belgium.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Bollards
metas.note:
Bollards are generally fairly rare in Bulgaria.

When you see them, they almost always have this somewhat generic design, which is relatively similar to the bollards found in Croatia and Hungary. They have a red reflector on the front, and a white one on the back. The design isn’t terribly consistent: sometimes they are thinner, and the shape of the reflector varies.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bulgaria.

metas.name: Cambodia - Road 4 Bollard
metas.note:
Unique triangular bollards with red stripes can be found in three places in Cambodia, all located in the same area in the southwest:

  • On Road 4 between Angk Snuol and Preah Sihanouk. They are especially common in the section between Kirirom National Park and Preah Sihanouk.
  • One small off-road of Road 4, in Ream National Park near Preah Sihanouk.
  • In Preah Monivong National Park.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cambodia.

metas.name: Cambodia - Road 48 Bollard
metas.note:
Black-and-white bollards in Cambodia are only found on Road 48, between Tatai and the intersection with Road 4.

NOTE: Make sure to check other clues before guessing, because this style of bollard is commonly found in Thailand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cambodia.

metas.name: Canada - Bollard
metas.note: Alberta has a unique black and white bollard that is often found at intersections. It has a cylindrical shape and two black bands that wrap all the way around. It is one of the most useful Canadian bollards to learn because it appears so frequently.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec guardrail Bollards
metas.note: Quebec has unique bollards that are always attached to guardrails. They are long, thin white poles with a red or green reflector at the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Saskatchewan & Manitoba Bollard
metas.note:
Manitoba uses black and grey painted bollards. Most of the time an orange stripe will be present below the grey one.

  • Wooden, rectangular bollards of this form are typically found further north in Manitoba

NOTE: Bollards in this format with just a black top are seen in Manitoba and Saskatchewan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Chile - Bollards
metas.note: Chilean bollards are similar to Spanish style bollards, with a white reflector at the front and a yellow-orange reflector at the back. They are not super common. While regular bollards are somewhat rare in Chile, you may sometimes find this orange, temporary bollard, with two white stripes at the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Colombia - Spanish bollard
metas.note: This spanish bollard is mostly found in Cundinamarca, the area surrounding Bogotá, but also on the 40 towards Villavicencio.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Croatia - Bollard
metas.note:
Croatian bollards are white with a black rectangle and red or white reflector. From the top, it is shaped like a triangle.

NOTE: The distance between the top end and the reflector is shorter than in Hungary.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Czechia/Slovakia - Bollards
metas.note: Bollards in Czechia and Slovakia have orange double reflectors on the front and a single white reflector on the back. There are also rarer blue and red variants.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Denmark - Bollard
metas.note:
Denmark has a very recognizable white bollard with a yellow reflector and a dark orange stripe. This bollard is unique to the country. You may also find this green variant.

NOTE: Belgium has bollards that may look somewhat similar. However, it will never feature the orange stripe.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/denmark.

metas.name: Ecuador - Bollards
metas.note:
Ecuador is one of the few Latin American countries where bollards are very common.

You will find two main types of bollards:

  • A round bollard with two red stripes,

  • A flat bollard with two red reflectors on black.

Many other bollards can be found, however, they will almost always have the same colour scheme and style.

NOTE: A similar rectangular bollard can sometimes be found in Malaysia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Estonia - Bollard
metas.note:
Round bollards with a rectangular reflector on the front and two circular reflectors on the back, which can be either white or orange, are common. Latvia's bollards might look similar, but they have a "half-circle" or flat curved shape, and sometimes feature numbers on them.

  • Baltic/Nordic bollard infographic
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/estonia.

metas.name: Faroe Islands - Bollards
metas.note: Faroese bollards are small wooden sticks that are mainly painted yellow and sometimes red on the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Finland - Bollards
metas.note:
Bollards in Finland are always completely black and white. They have a white rectangular reflector on the front and two white dots on the back. The black stripe is slightly angled.

They come in two shapes:

  • Hollow, thin and curved

  • Round, baton-like shape

  • Baltic/Nordic bollard infographic
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: Finland - Snow Pole
metas.note:
Orange snow pole with a thin white band near the top is commonly found in Finland. Norway/Sweden uses similar version but they have much wider white band (or even sometimes multiple ones).

  • Baltic/Nordic bollard infographic
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: France - Bollard
metas.note:
The French bollard is extremely recognizable and appears very often. It is a round white post with a pointed top and a reflector band going all the way around. The band can be grey or red. Some rare variations have a fully red top.

NOTE: A bollard that is commonly found in Scotland looks similar, but has a blunt top instead of a pointed one.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/france.

metas.name: Germany - Bollard
metas.note:
Germany uses these black and white bollards, with white and light-grey reflectors. The reflector will be orange on bollards next to intersections. They sometimes have plates containing the road number, and potentially other useful information. Many bollards also feature blue attachments on the side.

NOTE: Luxembourg uses almost identical bollards, but they have 3 bolts instead of 2 on the reflector. NOTE: Portugal also uses the same bollards as Germany, but you will not see such a blue reflector as the one in the image.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Greece - Bollard
metas.note:
Greek bollards are wedge-shaped with almost square reflectors, being red on the front and white on the back.

NOTE: Andorra bollards are similar but landscape/vegetation will be way different most of the time.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/greece.

metas.name: Hungary - Bollard
metas.note: Hungarian bollards are black-and-white, wedge-shaped, and typically have a red reflector at the front, and a white reflector at the back. Blue reflectors are also somewhat common.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/hungary.

metas.name: Iceland - Bollard
metas.note: Iceland has unique yellow bollards with a white reflector. These bollards are extremely common and can be found throughout the country on almost every section of rural road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/iceland.

metas.name: Indonesia - Bollards
metas.note:
Indonesia commonly uses these black-and-white square or circular bollards, as well as these yellow-and-black ones, which can also have a red reflector. Other designs can also be found.

NOTE: UK-style bollards are mostly found in Kalimantan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/indonesia.

metas.name: Italy - Bollard
metas.note:
Italian bollards are triangular in shape, and white with a black top. They have a red front and a white rear reflector.

NOTE: Albania uses the same bollards.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Japan - Akita Bollard
metas.note: This bollard, much like Tohoku, will be a thick, white bollard with an octagonal reflector. However, this Akita prefecture variation will have two yellow stripes underneath the reflector.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Aomori Bollard
metas.note: This bollard, found in the Aomori prefecture, has two yellow stripes, a single circular reflector, and is extendable. Sometimes, only one thicker stripe near the top may be present.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Bollards
metas.note: In Japan, simple white bollards with circular or rectangular reflectors at the top are commonly used. However, sometimes these bollards are black, or have other extensions. They can also have the city or prefecture written on it in kanji.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu/Yamaguchi Bollard
metas.note:
This flat, white bollard, found on the island of Kyushu and in Yamaguchi Prefecture, will have a series of separated orange reflectors on one side, and the same white on the opposite.

NOTE: Rarely, you may find similar bollards in Hokkaido. However, both sides will have orange reflectors.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Okayama Bollard
metas.note: This bollard, with an octagonal reflector, and red stripe underneath it, is exclusive to the Okayama prefecture. Additionally, there will be a sloped connection where the base meets the reflector.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Striped Bollard
metas.note: These striped bollards (which cover over the original) have a thinner top half, and no reflectors, and are common to the Tohoku region. They are especially common in Akita prefecture.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Tohoku Bollard
metas.note:
This thick, white bollard, found in the Tohoku region, will have an octagonal reflector, and yellow stripe just underneath. In addition, you can find the same bollard, but with a rectangular top.

Finally, there are two other variations. You can find a black octagonal, and rectangular version. They are often found on National Highways or Expressways and can have the number printed on them.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Toyama Bollard
metas.note:
The Toyama prefecture bollard has one reflector, is extendable and has a red stripe underneath the reflector.

NOTE: Be careful: if there is either a second reflector, or a yellow stripe instead of a red one, these are different bollards. These are more common variations found across many prefectures.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Bollards
metas.note: Kazakhstan uses a variety of post-Soviet style bollards, as well as ones that resemble Turkish bollards. Notably, the bollards seemingly consisting of two thin bollards attached at a 90° angle are unique to Kazakhstan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Bollard
metas.note: Kyrgyzstan uses these simple white bollards with a diagonal black stripe near the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan.

metas.name: Latvia - Bollard
metas.note:
Half-circle/flat curved shape bollards with a rectangular reflector on the front and two circular reflectors on the back are common. The reflectors can be white or orange, and sometimes these bollards have numbers on them.

Estonian bollards might look similar, but they have a rounded shape and will never have numbers on them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/latvia.

metas.name: Lithuania - Bollard
metas.note:
Lithuanian bollards are wedge-shaped.

They have an orange reflector on the front, and a white reflector on the back. Both reflectors are rectangular. You may find this thin version as well.

NOTE: Estonian and Latvian bollards look different.

NOTE: All nothern EU Bollards
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lithuania.

metas.name: Luxembourg - Bollard
metas.note:
Bollards are black and white. They are wedge-shaped and have grey reflectors. Some have a distinctive indent in the lower half. The bollards of Belgium, the Netherlands and France look very different.

NOTE: They look more or less identical to German bollards. The most notable difference is that the reflectors on German bollards have two bolts, while in Luxembourg they have three.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/luxembourg.

metas.name: Madeira - Stone Bollards
metas.note: Madeira commonly uses small and unique stone bollards with a red reflector. They are either cuboidal or cylindrical in shape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Malaysia - Bollards
metas.note:
Malaysian bollards will often have the colours black, white, grey and red. Here are three examples of typical Malaysian bollards.

NOTE: There can be multiple varieties of these bollards, but the layout is mostly the same.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Mexico - Bollard
metas.note: These small, cylindrical white bollards with a black base are unique to Mexico. A yellow reflector is sometimes seen, as well as a flat version.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Jalisco Bollard
metas.note: Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a crown and the text ‘Jalisco’ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Nayarit Bollard
metas.note: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mongolia - Bollard
metas.note: Mongolia uniquely features white bowling-pin shaped bollards with two red stripes around the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Namibia - Bollard
metas.note: These stone bollards are found in Namibia. They have a small reflector on top and are usually located behind these red and white reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/namibia for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Bollard
metas.note: The Netherlands has a simple, white or black bollard with a red and white reflector.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/netherlands.

metas.name: New Zealand - Bollard
metas.note: New Zealand has a unique white bollard with a red strip that wraps around the entire back and part of the front.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: North Macedonia - Bollards
metas.note: North Macedonia uses two types of bollards. One is rounded and very thin, while the other one is wedge-shaped(looks like Croatia bollard). They both are white and have red or white reflectors, typically on a black surface.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/north-macedonia.

metas.name: Norway - Bollards
metas.note:
Bollards in Norway are always completely black and white. They have a silver rectangular reflector on the front and two white dots on the back. The black stripe is slightly angled, and the bollards are narrow and flat.

  • Baltic/Nordic bollard infographic
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Bollards
metas.note:
Bollards in Peru are painted red or yellow, and the country mainly uses a variety of triangularshaped concrete bollards. Occasionally you will also spot other designs, such as these circular concrete variants.

NOTE: These concrete variants can also be found in Bolivia and Brazil so do not rule out these countries if you find such bollards.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Lima/Ica 1S Bollard
metas.note: These bollards are only found on the 1S highway between the towns of Ica and Lima.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Moquegua Bollard
metas.note: This cylindrical bollard, with a black and yellow stripe at the top, is unique to the state of Moquegua, which is located in the south of Peru.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - North Lima Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is only found on the 1N highway north of Lima (still within Lima region).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Tacna Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is almost exclusive to Tacna region. It does spill into Moquegua but it is by far most common in Tacna.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Bollard
metas.note:
Polish bollards have a red strip that wraps all the way around the bollard. This strip has a red reflector on the front (sometimes hard to see), and a white reflector on the back. Bollards sometimes have numbers on them.

NOTE: The same design can be found in Zakarpattia Oblast in Ukraine.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/poland.

metas.name: Portugal - Bollards
metas.note: Portuguese bollards are either wedge-shaped with a noticeably thin white top, or flat with a wide reflector. While most reflectors will be white, you may also find orange reflectors. These are noticeably darker than the yellow reflectors in Spain.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Romania - Bollard
metas.note:
Romanian bollards are thin and white, with a red vertical strip near the top. It is worth noting that bollards in Romania are somewhat rare.

NOTE: Turkey has a very similar bollard.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/romania.

metas.name: Russia - Bollards
metas.note: Russia has three main types of bollards: a very thin type being attached to a stick, one with a black top section and a red vertical reflector below and a German-style bollard.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Rwanda - Bollards
metas.note: Rwanda uses multiple different red and white cylindrical bollards.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: Senegal - French Bollards
metas.note: The Senegal/French bollard is extremely recognizable and appears very often. It is a round white post with a pointed top and a reflector band going all the way around. The band can be grey or red. Some rare variations have a fully red top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Serbia - Bollards
metas.note: Serbian bollards might look like Austria/Slovenia bollards but reflector will be always off-center. They have couple other designs but reflector will be always off-center.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/serbia.

metas.name: Slovenia - Bollard
metas.note:
Slovenian bollards are white with a black top. The front reflector will typically be bright red, while the back reflector will be white.

NOTE: Austrian bollards have the same design, but with a dark red front reflector and a black or grey back reflector. Montenegrin bollards also have a very similar design, also with a red and a white reflector.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovenia.

metas.name: South Korea - Bollard
metas.note: You will sometimes see these black and white wedge-shaped bollards. They have a round yellow reflector on the front, and a grey one on the back.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-korea.

metas.name: Spain - Aragón Bollard
metas.note:
In Aragón, it is common to see this bollard design on regional roads.

It has a simple design, consisting of a short flat rectangular white stick with a grey reflector on both sides.

NOTE: There are similar bollards in other regions, but they appear much less frequently than in Aragón.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Bollard
metas.note:
The standard Spanish bollards have a yellow-orange reflector on the front and two white dots on the back (though the back can also be blank). They are typically hollow.

NOTE: Very close to Andorra, you can find a slightly different bollard, which is also used in Andorra itself.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Extremadura Bollard
metas.note: In the region of Extremadura, it is common to see the normal Spanish bollards with green tops. This bollard variant is exclusive to this region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Bollard
metas.note: These short, wide stone bollards are unique to Sri Lanka. They have a tapered shape, with a black base and a white top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Bollards
metas.note:
Sweden has variety of Bollards. The most common ones are:

  • The standart bollard: wedge-shaped, similar to german bollards, can be yellow/orange
  • Another common bollard: round, baton-like shaped, reflectors are the same as the wedge-shaped bollard, black strip is straight
  • Another common bollard: black strip, that doesn't go all the way around, reflector tends to be more silver, more commonly thin and curverd, baton shaped versions exist
  • Baltic/Nordic bollard infographic
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Switzerland - Bollards
metas.note:
Swiss bollards are black-and-white with white or grey reflectors. They can be either wedge-shaped or cylindrical with a rounded top.

NOTE: Liechtenstein uses almost identical round bollards.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/switzerland.

metas.name: Taiwan - Bollards
metas.note:
Taiwan uses these bollards with either two or three circular reflectors on a black rectangle.

You can also find these lollipop looking reflectors on guardrails, similar to the designs found in Japan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Thailand - Bollards
metas.note:
The Thai bollard is square shaped with a pointed top, and has black-and-white and red-and-white stripes.

NOTE: In Southeast Asia, these bollards are also found in Cambodia, Laos and Indonesia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Turkey - Bollard
metas.note: Turkish bollards are white and rectangular with a red reflector on the front, making them quite unique. Similar bollards exist in Romania but are very rare. Australian bollards typically have a reflector on the back and a slightly different design.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Ukraine - Polish Bollards
metas.note:
These “Polish” bollards can be found in the Zakarpattia Oblast. They have a red reflector that wraps around the bollard.

They are identical to the standard bollard used in Poland (hence the name).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Bollard
metas.note: The most common bollard in the UK looks like this. It has a rounded shape, with a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back. The base and top are black, with a white stripe in the middle.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scotland Bollard
metas.note:
In Scotland, you can often find these red and white bollards. They are round, bulky, and have a red-and-grey reflector that wraps all the way around.

  • They are sometimes found in other parts of the UK.

NOTE: The bollard looks similar to the French one. However, there are some small differences. For example, the Scottish bollard is round on the top, while the French one is more spiked.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United States - Idaho/Utah Bollard
metas.note: This thin bollard with a small white reflector at the top is unique to Utah and Idaho
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Montana/South Dakota Bollard
metas.note:
The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.

NOTE: These bollards can be found to a lesser extent in other western states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Nevada Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Oregon Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is unique to Oregon state in US.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Washington Bollard
metas.note: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Western Bollards
metas.note:
These bollards are found in the upper western states from Utah to Washington.

  • The white version is more common in Washington, Oregon and Idaho

  • The green version is more common in Montana, Idaho and Utah

  • The black version is more common in Wyoming, Utah, South Dakota and colorado

NOTE: Technically, all colors can be found in every western state, but the likelihood of finding them is higher in the states listed.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Wyoming Bollard
metas.note: Roadside bollards in Wyoming often feature a dark metal pole with a white circular reflector at the top. The top of the metal pole is sometimes painted white or grey, which is unique to Wyoming
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: Uruguay - Bollard
metas.note: These white bollards, with one side often painted yellow, and stone barriers, are specific to Uruguay.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.

metas.name: Vietnam - Bollards
metas.note: In Vietnam, one type of bollard is primarily used. This bollard is white with a red tip and a yellow reflector on the front. However, a Spanish-type bollard made of stone can also rarely be found.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/vietnam for more clues.
